methods_search: The original comparison used the fixed configurations documented in Table~\ref{tab:model_config}; their initial selection rationale could not be independently established, and we do not claim an original systematic search. A separate revision sensitivity analysis used validation-based selection. XGBoost searched 27 combinations of tree count, learning rate and depth; BiLSTM-Attention searched 27 combinations of recurrent units, learning rate and dropout. Seed 42 screened each grid, the top three were rechecked with seeds 42, 123 and 7, and the selected and original configurations were evaluated with five seeds. Transformer and the three Gaussian recurrent models instead received only a three-learning-rate search at seed 42, selecting by validation RMSE for Transformer and full-validation Gaussian CRPS for the probabilistic models. Every candidate retained test metrics, but the archived selection rules use validation scores only. The search spaces and budgets are not equal across models (Supplementary Table~\ref{supp-stab:r2m9_search}).
methods_groups: Within this sensitivity analysis, A denotes the original settings and epoch cap, B the original settings with a longer cap, and C the validation-selected settings with that longer cap. BiLSTM-Attention used caps 30 and 60; the other neural models used 30 and 100, with early-stopping patience 10. XGBoost has A=B. The A references for the neural models are q21/q14 reruns, not a replacement for the complete original Table~\ref{tab:seed_stability} run set. Paired differences compare seed-level scores, using the same five seeds and test targets. Separate pointwise 95\% seed-$t$ and moving-block percentile intervals use four degrees of freedom and 28-sample blocks, 5,000 replicates and resampling seed 42, respectively. Sampled indices are truncated to the test length before applying rainfall masks; within-seed score differences are then averaged, rather than averaging predictions first. A descriptive three-way improvement criterion requires all five seeds to improve and both intervals to lie below zero; it is not a multiplicity correction (Supplementary Table~\ref{supp-stab:r2m9_effects}).
results: In the q19 sensitivity cohort, the six-model RMSE ordering was unchanged between A and C for the full, revised-wet and upper-tail test subsets. The overall BiLSTM-Attention advantage over XGBoost nevertheless narrowed from 0.001057 to 0.000161~mm\,h$^{-1}$. Validation-selected BiLSTM-Attention had slightly higher overall RMSE (+0.06\%), while XGBoost upper-tail RMSE increased by 0.26\%, with no seed showing improvement. Transformer improved numerically by 0.78\% from A to B and a further 0.59\% from B to C, giving 1.37\% overall; its seed interval still included zero. Only BU-LSTM-Attention CRPS improvement met the three-way rule (1.73\% lower). These rankings concern the q19 A/C collections: in A, BU-LSTM precedes BU-LSTM-Attention, unlike their order in the original Table~\ref{tab:seed_stability}. Both interval types and unfavourable effects are retained in Supplementary Table~\ref{supp-stab:r2m9_effects}.
cost: The 117 unique q19 task records sum to 3.87~h. Their timer covers model construction, fitting and validation/test prediction up to its stop; it is not pure fit time, an end-to-end search wall-clock measurement or GPU-hours. The XGBoost execution device and separate inference cost were not recorded. This total excludes the earlier q21/q14 A-reference runs. Per-model counts, recorded task times and validation candidate rankings are given in Supplementary Table~\ref{supp-stab:r2m9_search}.
discussion: The sensitivity analysis does not establish equal-budget optimization or globally optimal original settings. The Transformer A-to-B change shows that the original epoch cap constrained some runs, while its combined improvement does not meet the three-way rule. The two leading models remain close after tuning. BiLSTM-Attention\textquotesingle s best two three-seed validation means differ by only 0.000053~mm\,h$^{-1}$, so the selected configuration should not be interpreted as decisively superior. The original no-attention BiLSTM was not included in q19 tuning; these results therefore do not establish an optimally tuned attention-versus-no-attention benefit.
limitations: The q19 search is a retrospective sensitivity analysis on one existing chronological split, with unequal search spaces and different validation selection objectives. Candidate test scores were stored, so validation-only selection does not turn this into a new, untouched model-development test. The intervals are pointwise and unadjusted for multiple comparisons. Search uncertainty and computational cost do not exhaust model-design uncertainty, and the conclusions are restricted to the tested configurations, data split and regional target.
